The main challenges and how you solved them
The results and why you feel proud

phrases.meaning: reach a problem that stops progress

model: The project I'm proudest of is a training programme I built for new staff at the marketing agency where I work. I've been at the company for four years, and for most of that time, new employees just learned by watching others, which was pretty chaotic. So last year my manager asked me to take the lead on creating a proper onboarding course. We had a tight deadline of about two months, and we had to build everything from scratch, including videos, quizzes and a simple handbook. At first, it went well, but halfway through we hit a wall because the videos were taking much longer to edit than we'd planned. Then the whole team really pulled together. A couple of designers stayed late to help, and I learned to use editing software I'd never touched before. In the end, we launched it on time, and I've been updating it ever since. Since then, around thirty new people have gone through the course, and the feedback has exceeded expectations. New staff say they feel confident much sooner, and managers have told me they spend less time answering basic questions. I think I'm proud of it because it was the first time I'd managed something that big, and all the hard work really paid off. It gave me a real sense of achievement, and it's made me want to take on more leadership roles.
